input.quote: (a) This Agreement is governed in all respects by the laws of the State of Delaware without giving effect to its conflict of laws principles. Each Party hereby irrevocably submits for all disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in New York, New York.
input.rationale: Section 14(a) picks Delaware law (a fallback-acceptable choice) but pairs it with exclusive venue in the New York courts, so the law/forum pairing does not match either checklist level. More materially, Section 8 mandates that "[a]ny controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach thereof, shall be settled by arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association," which contradicts and displaces the exclusive court jurisdiction in 14(a). With disputes routed to arbitration rather than courts, the fallback dispute-forum element fails on a material term. Because the existing venue is already New York, the shortest coherent fix is the preferred position: New York law, exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, and deletion of the mandatory arbitration sentence (the jury-trial waiver and one-year limitation period in Section 8 are left intact).

proposal.summary: Move governing law to New York, fix New York County venue, and remove the conflicting mandatory AAA arbitration mechanic.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have moved the governing law to New York (our playbook's preferred position) and confirmed exclusive venue in the state and federal courts in New York County. We also deleted the mandatory AAA arbitration sentence, which contradicts that exclusive court jurisdiction; the jury-trial waiver and limitation period are unchanged.
